lines: EC2: Renting a Computer by the Hour

blocks.ava_speaks: Welcome to CS1B! Shared Responsibility Model முடிச்சிட்டீங்க. Super. But cloud-ல real-ஆ வேலை செய்ய, we need to understand the 5 core pillars of AWS. Let's start with the most famous one: Amazon EC2.
blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: EC2 stands for 'Elastic Compute Cloud'. Jargon-அ விடுங்க. Simply put, EC2-னா renting a computer over the internet. Physical hardware வாங்காம, AWS data center-ல இருக்கிற ஒரு server-அ நாம hourly rent-க்கு எடுக்குறோம்.

blocks.ava_speaks: Why rent? Think about JioCinema streaming the IPL final. அன்னைக்கு மட்டும் 3 கோடி பேர் live-ஆ பாப்பாங்க. அந்த scale-அ handle பண்ண, they need massive computing power.
blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: 3 கோடி பேருக்கு physical servers வாங்குனா, IPL முடிஞ்சதும் அந்த servers சும்மா தான் இருக்கும். Crores of rupees wasted on hardware sitting in a dark room. That is how traditional IT worked. It was a nightmare.
blocks.speaker: Ren

blocks.ava_speaks: Instead, they use EC2. Match start ஆகும்போது ஆயிரக்கணக்கான virtual servers-அ வாடகைக்கு (rent) எடுப்பாங்க. Match முடிஞ்சதும் திருப்பி குடுத்துருவாங்க. You only pay for exactly what you use. This magic is called 'Elasticity'.

board_actions.text: Scale UP: Add servers instantly when traffic spikes.
Scale DOWN: Remove servers when traffic drops.

blocks.ava_speaks: When you rent this virtual server (we call it an 'Instance'), you don't just get a generic computer. You get to pick its brain. You choose the exact CPU and RAM. Video rendering-ஆ? Pick a high-CPU instance. Database running-ஆ? Pick high-RAM.

workspace_tasks.question: Swiggy is preparing for New Year's Eve (Dec 31st). They expect a 15x spike in food orders between 7 PM and 1 AM. What is the most cost-effective and reliable compute architecture for this 6-hour window?
options: Buy high-end physical servers for their on-premise data center to handle the 15x traffic securely.
Pre-configure their EC2 instances to automatically scale up (add more servers) at 6 PM, and scale down at 2 AM.
Upload the API as static files only — no virtual servers — and hope traffic somehow gets served.
Upgrade to a single, massive EC2 instance permanently so they never have to worry about traffic spikes again.
workspace_tasks.ava_feedback_correct: Dec 31st only 15x traffic. Permanent- physical server, No EC2 instance- run do massive money waste. EC2 'Elasticity' use do scale up/down doing real engineering.
workspace_tasks.ava_feedback_wrong: Dec 31st only 15x traffic. Permanent- physical server, No EC2 instance- run do massive money waste. EC2 'Elasticity' use do scale up/down doing real engineering.
workspace_tasks.explanation: Dec 31st only 15x traffic. Permanent- physical server, No EC2 instance- run do massive money waste. EC2 'Elasticity' use do scale up/down doing real engineering.

workspace_tasks.question: A junior developer says, 'We need to deploy our new Node.js backend API — just leave the code files sitting somewhere, we don't need an EC2 instance.' Why is Ren going to reject this proposal?
options: Because Node.js doesn't run on AWS.
Because a backend API needs a virtual computer (EC2) to actually RUN the code — storing files alone is not compute.
Because the backend API code needs an IAM policy to compute.
Because EC2 cannot handle backend APIs.
workspace_tasks.ava_feedback_correct: Backend code run do 'Compute' (Brain) is needed. EC2 is that compute — the virtual server that executes your API. Files code run. Always match the tool to the right problem.
